clue.text: Speak sincerely, at home anyway, about taking us in

indicators.note: to take something in is to admit it inside, so the extra word goes within the phrase
about suggests turning things around and mixing them, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone urges honest talk among the family, at home at least, about something that involves us.
explanation.walkthrough: Comma and all, 'at home anyway' reads like a qualifier, but its twelve letters plus US are the whole fodder for MEAN WHAT YOU SAY.
explanation.definitionFit: To talk sincerely is to have real intent behind your words, which is exactly the idiom's sense.

clue.text: Fall short coming up by Friday with loan to cover our chum

indicators.note: short means cut down, so the final letter of that season is dropped
in a down clue, coming up means read from bottom to top, so the shortened word runs backwards
to cover something is to lie around it, so the day abbreviation sits inside

blocks.note: fall is the American word for that season
a loan is what you lend; the verb form
the standard abbreviation of the weekday

explanation.surface: Someone short of cash on Friday borrows from a friend to tide things over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fall' looks like a verb going with 'short', but it is the American name for the season; 'our chum' is a friend shared by two people.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who is friends with both of us is a shared pal, so 'our chum' describes a companion common to two people.

clue.text: Violence is on the rise in some cyborg games

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means read upward, so the letters run backwards
in some of the words means the answer is tucked inside a run of these letters

blocks.note: the letters spanning the two words, ignoring the space

explanation.surface: A complaint that video games about cyborgs are getting ever more violent.
explanation.walkthrough: Aggro is British slang, short for aggravation, meaning trouble or aggressive behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for aggressive, troublesome behaviour or fighting, which matches brutal physical force.

clue.text: Justified conflict with journalist after verbal attack

blocks.note: a war is armed conflict
a rant is a loud angry tirade
ED, short for editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A journalist's piece follows a war of words, suggesting the fight was deserved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places the journalist behind the verbal attack, so ED comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: Something warranted has good grounds or authority behind it, the same as being justified.

clue.text: Alters notices about fair

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the notices wrap around the word for fair

blocks.note: ads are advertisements or public notices
fair and just both mean even-handed

explanation.surface: Someone changes the wording of announcements concerning a funfair.
explanation.definitionFit: To adjust is to make small changes to something, so it is a synonym for modifies.

clue.text: Wild hog breaks into tent to find food

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so these letters are scrambled
breaking into a place means getting inside it, so the scrambled letters go within

blocks.note: taken as written
a yurt is a round felt tent of Central Asian nomads

explanation.surface: A wild boar raids a campsite tent in search of something to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Yoghurt is a dairy product eaten as a snack or dessert, an example of food in general.

clue.text: Out until dark

indicators.note: out can mean disordered or wrong, signalling that the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is staying out on the town until night falls.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with no lamps or lights switched on stays without illumination, hence gloomy and black.

clue.text: Newsreader can run one broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast also means scattered widely like seed, so the letters are spread and rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A presenter is capable of fronting a programme on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' sits naturally beside a newsreader, but it is the signal to scatter the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: On radio and television, the person who reads out bulletins and introduces programmes is a presenter of news.

clue.text: Row about finally trapping wild cat

indicators.note: finally points to the very last letter of the next word
about means placed around, so the row encloses the chosen letter

blocks.note: a tier is a row of seats, one above another
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A quarrel arises over finally catching a dangerous big cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' tempts as a quarrel, but here it is a tier of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: The striped big cat of Asia is a feral feline living untamed in jungle and forest.

clue.text: Judge's ruling doesn't begin to cover horse in circus act

indicators.note: not beginning means the opening letter is lost
covering something means going around it, so the horse word sits inside

blocks.note: J is the abbreviation for judge
taken as written before its head is removed
gee-gee is a childish word for a horse

explanation.surface: A judge rules on whether a horse in a circus act should be covered up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Judge's ruling' reads as one phrase, but the judge supplies only a single letter and the ruling is a separate word to behead.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping several balls or clubs aloft at once is a classic ring performance by a clown or entertainer.

clue.text: Doubly bashful when sick and everyone comes in to hum and haw

indicators.note: coming in means entering, so these words go inside the shy ones

blocks.note: bashful means shy, and doubly means twice over
sick and ill are synonyms
all means every person

explanation.surface: A timid person feeling unwell dithers as a crowd arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doubly' means the bashful word is written twice, with one insertion going into each copy.
explanation.definitionFit: To shilly-shally is to dither and hesitate, just as someone hums and haws when undecided.

clue.text: Ask about acquiring girl's jackets

indicators.note: about suggests a turnaround, so the first word's letters are rearranged
acquiring means taking in, so the name goes inside the rearranged letters

blocks.note: taken as written
Nora is a girl's name; the apostrophe-s is surface glue

explanation.surface: Someone enquires about borrowing a young woman's coats.
explanation.definitionFit: Anoraks are hooded waterproof coats, so they are examples of outer garments for the upper body.

clue.text: Aunt ruthlessly conceals lie

indicators.note: what is concealed lies inside, so the answer is tucked within the words before it

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words, ignoring the space

explanation.surface: A heartless aunt hides a falsehood.
explanation.definitionFit: A falsehood is a statement that is not true, so a fib is the same thing.

clue.text: Feeble play on the radio

indicators.note: radio is heard, not seen, so the word is judged by how it sounds

blocks.note: a feint is a deceptive move or bit of play in boxing or fencing

explanation.surface: A critic dismisses a weak radio drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' looks like a drama to go with the radio, but it is a feint, a dummy move.
explanation.definitionFit: Weak and barely perceptible, as a voice or effort can be, which matches feeble.

clue.text: Soon unite main components

indicators.note: components are parts to be assembled, so the letters are put together in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Instructions to bring the principal parts together shortly.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means very shortly or before long, an idiom for something happening presently.

clue.text: Ridiculing pathetic racialist

indicators.note: pathetic means in a sorry state, so the letters are in poor order and need rearranging

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Mocking a contemptible bigot.
explanation.definitionFit: Satire uses mockery and irony to expose folly, so satirical writing is mocking in tone.

clue.text: Pragmatic about boxer with short fuse

indicators.note: short means cut off, so the last letter of the word for fuse is lost

blocks.note: re means concerning or about
Muhammad Ali, the famous heavyweight
to fuse things is to join or bond them

explanation.surface: A sensible view of a hot-tempered prizefighter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short fuse' suggests a quick temper, but fuse is a verb meaning join, cut short by one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Being practical and sensible about what can actually be achieved is a matter-of-fact outlook.

clue.text: At home, a horribly bullied student's withdrawn and silent

indicators.note: withdrawn means taken away, so the learner's letter is removed
horribly suggests something badly mangled, so the remaining letters are rearranged

blocks.note: someone at home is in
taken as written
taken as written before the learner is taken out
L for learner, as on a learner driver's plate; the 's means has

explanation.surface: A student badly picked on at home has become withdrawn and quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'withdrawn' reads as shy and quiet, but it tells you to take one L out of BULLIED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that cannot be heard makes no sound a listener can pick up, so it is effectively quiet.

clue.text: Catch up with trio taking break for Mexican food

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from bottom to top, so the word for catch runs backwards
break means smash apart, so the letters of the trio are rearranged

blocks.note: the rub is the catch or snag, as in 'there's the rub'
taken as written

explanation.surface: Three friends on a break meet up to grab some Mexican food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catch up' looks like meeting friends; split it into a word and its reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A burrito is a tortilla wrapped around a filling, a dish from Mexican cuisine.

clue.text: Made certain spaces suitable for all having wine

blocks.note: an en is a printer's space half an em wide
U is the British film certificate for universal viewing
red is a type of wine

explanation.surface: Someone checked there were rooms fit for every guest, wine included.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British film rating meaning suitable for all ages.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensure something is to guarantee it happens, so the past tense means guaranteed or secured.

clue.text: Display of top-grade river fish

blocks.note: A is the highest grade
R is the map abbreviation for river
a ray is a flat sea fish

explanation.surface: A fishmonger's showcase of the finest river catch.
explanation.definitionFit: An array is an impressive arranged show or range of things, the same as an exhibition.

clue.text: Fix counter in place for a manicure

blocks.note: to nail something is to fix it in place
a bar is a counter where drinks are served

explanation.surface: Instructions to attach a shop counter in a beauty salon.
explanation.definitionFit: A small salon offering fingernail treatments, painting and shaping is where people get hands done.

clue.text: Graduate's robes regularly get gibes

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate
first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: A graduate's gown is mocked at the ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbs are cutting, hurtful remarks, the same as taunts or jeers.

clue.text: Cook panics getting hot food for Popeye

indicators.note: to cook something is to alter it, so these letters are reworked

blocks.note: taken as written
H for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A chef flaps while serving a hot dish to the cartoon sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Popeye the Sailor famously eats tins of this leafy green vegetable to become super-strong.

clue.text: Kitchen range's popular once more

blocks.note: an Aga is a British brand of large heat-storage cooker
something in fashion is in

explanation.surface: Big old-fashioned cookers are back in fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: An Aga is the classic cast-iron range cooker of British country kitchens.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something a further time is repeating it, so the adverb means one more occasion.

clue.text: Question to annoy, arousing ire in stranger

indicators.note: arousing means stirring up, so the letters of the angry word are mixed

blocks.note: QU is a standard abbreviation for question
to irk is to irritate
taken as written

explanation.surface: Interrogating someone to irritate them, stirring anger in a newcomer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stranger' looks like a person, but it is the comparative adjective, more odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Quirky means odd or peculiar, so its comparative means more odd or more peculiar.

clue.text: Follow path

blocks.note: first meaning: to track or shadow someone
second meaning: a track through countryside

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to track or tail somebody, and as a noun it is a rough track or footway.

clue.text: Feeling for propriety and taste perhaps, regarding study about church and the limits of charity

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the study goes around the church abbreviation
limits are the edges, so only the first and last letters of the word are used

blocks.note: taste is one of the five senses, hence 'perhaps'
of can mean concerning, as in 'speak of'
a den is a private study or retreat
CE is the Church of England
the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A study of church charity, describing good manners and refined judgement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taste perhaps' marks taste as one example of the five senses; CE, the Church of England, is a common crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: An instinct for what is proper and respectable behaviour is an awareness of moral standards.
